candidates.old:
LDA sprites_y_offset,Y
    STA dm_raise
    TAY                             \ Y = the raise, for mark_part2 and ren_draw_sprite
    LDA dm_frame                    \ (C still clear: frame <= &3F plus an offset <= &1E)
    ADC mover_types_first_sprite_animation_offsets + &1C,X    \ the second parts' mover types
    TAX
    LDA animation_table,X
    JSR mark_part2
    JSR ren_draw_sprite
    LDX dm_type
    LDA mover_types_parts,X
    BEQ part_three                  \ three parts
.nothing
    RTS                             \ one part or two
.part_three
    LDA dm_raise                    \ part three: eight rows above part two
    CLC
    ADC #&08
    TAY
candidates.new:
LDA sprites_y_offset,Y
    TAY                             \ Y = the raise, for mark_part2 and ren_draw_sprite
    ADC #&08                        \ (C clear) dm_raise: part three's raise, eight rows above
    STA dm_raise                    \ (C still clear: the raise <= &F7)
    LDA dm_frame                    \ (C still clear: frame <= &3F plus an offset <= &1E)
    ADC mover_types_first_sprite_animation_offsets + &1C,X    \ the second parts' mover types
    TAX
    LDA animation_table,X
    JSR mark_part2
    JSR ren_draw_sprite
    LDX dm_type
    LDA mover_types_parts,X
    BEQ part_three                  \ three parts
.nothing
    RTS                             \ one part or two
    EQUB &EA, &EA                   \ never run: keeps the code after it where it was
.part_three
    LDY dm_raise                    \ part three: eight rows above part two (stored so)
candidates.summary: Store part three's raise (raise+8) in dm_raise during part two (one ADC #8, C known clear), so part three is LDY dm_raise instead of LDA/CLC/ADC #8/TAY; the 2 bytes saved are padded after the RTS so nothing after the window moves. Alternative to the next candidate.
candidates.equivalence: dm_raise is written only here and read only at part_three (grep: declared game.6502:5430, no other reference in src/); it now holds raise+8 instead of raise, so part three's Y is identical. In part two C is clear after ADC mover_types_second_sprite_offset,X (the existing code already relies on it); LDA/TAY leave C, so ADC #8 adds exactly 8 and leaves C clear because sprites_y_offset's bytes (and those the index can reach after it: the helicopter tables, max &EC) are all <= &F7, so the following ADC first+&1C,X still sees C=0 as before. Y passed to mark_part2/ren_draw_sprite is the raise as before (TAY before the ADC). A after the STA is reloaded by LDA dm_frame. Two-part movers: dm_raise is dead after (never read). Part three: Y = dm_raise = raise+8 as old TAY gave; A is reloaded by the next line LDA mover_types_third_sprite,X (outside the window, unchanged); flags overwritten by that LDA; C unused by mark_part3 (PHA..SEC..PLA) and ren_draw_sprite (TAX first, sets C itself before use). X unchanged (dm_type). Interrupt never reads dm_raise (renderer workspace).
candidates.relies_on: sprites_y_offset entries reachable (frame+second offset) are <= &F7 so ADC #8 leaves C clear (table max &17; the bytes after it max &EC). Layout: .nothing moves &9B24->&9B26, part_three &9B25->&9B29, LDA mover_types_third_sprite stays at &9B2B and everything after is unmoved; BCS nothing (&9B00, next &9B02) and BEQ part_three (&9B24, next &9B26) still land in page &9B, no new crossing. Part two (1.1/pass) +2 cycles, part three (1.1/pass) -6 cycles, from the window's measured counts (BEQ part_three always taken).
